scenes.tts: Radial glial fibres guide young neurons outward. Are those same cells also the source of the neurons?
scenes.visual: Title card fades. A young neuron climbs a radial fibre. Question on screen: scaffold or source?
scenes.narration: Radial glial fibres guide young neurons outward. Are those same cells also the source of the neurons?

scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy-two, Pasko Rakic studied fetal rhesus monkey cortex. He found young neurons pressed against radial fibres.
scenes.caption: In 1972, Pasko Rakic studied fetal rhesus monkey cortex. He found young neurons pressed against radial fibres.
scenes.visual: A thick fetal monkey cortical wall. Golgi-filled cells and an electron micrograph inset show a neuron against a fibre. Tag: Rakic, 1972.
scenes.narration: In 1972, Pasko Rakic studied fetal rhesus monkey cortex. He found young neurons pressed against radial fibres.

scenes.tts: Radial glia were seen mainly as scaffolds. Neurons, it was thought, came from some other cell in the ventricular zone.
scenes.visual: The fibre is labelled scaffold. A grey unnamed cell at the ventricle is labelled source?
scenes.narration: Radial glia were seen mainly as scaffolds. Neurons, it was thought, came from some other cell in the ventricular zone.

scenes.tts: Around the year two thousand, three lines of evidence in rodents, using four methods, changed the picture. Each asked the question a different way.
scenes.caption: Around the year 2000, three lines of evidence in rodents, using four methods, changed the picture. Each asked the question a different way.
scenes.visual: An empty table with four rows: sorting, fate map, filming, recording. Columns: if only a scaffold, what was seen.
scenes.narration: Around the year 2000, three lines of evidence in rodents, using four methods, changed the picture. Each asked the question a different way.

scenes.tts: For each one, ask: if radial glia were only a scaffold, what would we see?
scenes.visual: The column if only a scaffold is highlighted.
scenes.narration: For each one, ask: if radial glia were only a scaffold, what would we see?

scenes.tts: First, sorting, in mouse. The Götz group used mice that make G F P from a human G F A P promoter.
scenes.caption: First, sorting, in mouse. The Götz group used mice that make GFP from a human GFAP promoter.
scenes.visual: Mouse cortex in which radial glia glow green. Label: GFP from a human GFAP promoter.
scenes.narration: First, sorting, in mouse. The Götz group used mice that make GFP from a human GFAP promoter.

scenes.tts: Rodent radial glia make little G F A P protein. But that human promoter fragment is active in them.
scenes.caption: Rodent radial glia make little GFAP protein. But that human promoter fragment is active in them.
scenes.visual: Side note: rodent radial glia, little GFAP protein; human GFAP promoter fragment, active.
scenes.narration: Rodent radial glia make little GFAP protein. But that human promoter fragment is active in them.

scenes.tts: The green cells were sorted into a dish. If they were only scaffolds, you might expect few or no neurons. Did they make any?
scenes.visual: Green cells stream through a sorter into a dish. Row 1, if only a scaffold: few or no neurons expected.
scenes.narration: The green cells were sorted into a dish. If they were only scaffolds, you might expect few or no neurons. Did they make any?

scenes.tts: In culture, they made neurons. But a dish shows potential, not fate.
scenes.visual: Neurons appear in the dish. Row 1, seen: made neurons. Blind spot: potential, not fate.
scenes.narration: In culture, they made neurons. But a dish shows potential, not fate.

scenes.tts: Second, fate mapping in the living mouse. An enzyme called Cree recombinase was made from a G F A P promoter.
scenes.caption: Second, fate mapping in the living mouse. An enzyme called Cre recombinase was made from a GFAP promoter.
scenes.visual: A living mouse embryo. Label: Cre recombinase from a GFAP promoter.
scenes.narration: Second, fate mapping in the living mouse. An enzyme called Cre recombinase was made from a GFAP promoter.

scenes.tts: Cree cuts out a stop sequence in front of a reporter gene. The cut is a change in the DNA.
scenes.caption: Cre cuts out a stop sequence in front of a reporter gene. The cut is a change in the DNA.
scenes.visual: A DNA strip: promoter, STOP box, reporter. Scissors remove the STOP box.
scenes.narration: Cre cuts out a stop sequence in front of a reporter gene. The cut is a change in the DNA.

scenes.tts: So it is copied into every descendant, even after the promoter switches off in a neuron.
scenes.visual: The cut DNA copies into each daughter cell; a neuron keeps glowing though its promoter light goes off.
scenes.narration: So it is copied into every descendant, even after the promoter switches off in a neuron.

scenes.tts: If radial glia were only scaffolds, cortical neurons would stay dark. What did the fate map show?
scenes.visual: Row 2, if only a scaffold: cortical neurons dark. The cortex waits, unlit.
scenes.narration: If radial glia were only scaffolds, cortical neurons would stay dark. What did the fate map show?

scenes.tts: Nearly all cortical projection neurons carried the reporter. Cortical interneurons, local inhibitory cells, did not. They are born in the ventral forebrain.
scenes.visual: The cortex lights up with labelled projection neurons; a few unlabelled interneurons arrive from below, tagged ventral forebrain. Row 2, seen.
scenes.narration: Nearly all cortical projection neurons carried the reporter. Cortical interneurons, local inhibitory cells, did not. They are born in the ventral forebrain.

scenes.tts: Third, filming lineage, in rat. A retrovirus carrying G F P was injected into the ventricles.
scenes.caption: Third, filming lineage, in rat. A retrovirus carrying GFP was injected into the ventricles.
scenes.visual: Rat embryo brain; a needle into the ventricle. Label: GFP retrovirus.
scenes.narration: Third, filming lineage, in rat. A retrovirus carrying GFP was injected into the ventricles.

scenes.tts: This retrovirus enters only dividing cells, and these cells divide right at the ventricle. Every descendant of a marked cell inherits the mark.
scenes.visual: Green virus particles at the ventricle; a rounded, dividing cell there turns green. One green cell in a living slice; a film-strip border appears.
scenes.narration: This retrovirus enters only dividing cells, and these cells divide right at the ventricle. Every descendant of a marked cell inherits the mark.

scenes.tts: A green radial glial cell divides at the ventricle. It keeps its fibre.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse: the green cell rounds at the ventricle and divides; its fibre stays in place.
scenes.narration: A green radial glial cell divides at the ventricle. It keeps its fibre.

scenes.tts: Its daughter becomes a neuron and moves out along a parental fibre. In mouse, Miyata and colleagues saw a newborn neuron inherit the fibre itself.
scenes.visual: The daughter climbs a parental fibre. Row 3, seen. Tag: Noctor and colleagues, rat, 2001. Inset: a mouse neuronal daughter inherits the parent's fibre and pulls itself up along it; tag Miyata and colleagues, mouse, 2001.
scenes.narration: Its daughter becomes a neuron and moves out along a parental fibre. In mouse, Miyata and colleagues saw a newborn neuron inherit the fibre itself.

scenes.tts: Last, recording, in rat. Precursors were recorded with an electrode, then filled with dye.
scenes.visual: An electrode touches a cell; dye fills it.
scenes.narration: Last, recording, in rat. Precursors were recorded with an electrode, then filled with dye.

scenes.tts: The filled cells had the shape of radial glia. Radial glial markers labeled nearly all cells caught in S phase or mitosis.
scenes.visual: The filled cell shows a long radial fibre. Row 4, seen: radial glial shape; markers on nearly all dividing cells.
scenes.narration: The filled cells had the shape of radial glia. Radial glial markers labeled nearly all cells caught in S phase or mitosis.

scenes.tts: Each method has a blind spot. A dish shows potential. An electrode samples only cells it can reach. A marker is not a family tree.
scenes.visual: The blind spot column fills, one row at a time.
scenes.narration: Each method has a blind spot. A dish shows potential. An electrode samples only cells it can reach. A marker is not a family tree.

scenes.tts: But the blind spots differ. And every result went against a scaffold-only view. The fate map and the films showed neuronal ancestry directly.
scenes.visual: The whole table glows; the if only a scaffold column is struck through. The fate-map and filming rows are highlighted: ancestry seen.
scenes.narration: But the blind spots differ. And every result went against a scaffold-only view. The fate map and the films showed neuronal ancestry directly.

scenes.tts: So in embryonic rodent cortex, the cell that guides migrating neurons is also the cell that makes most of them.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: in rodent cortex, the guide is also the source.
scenes.narration: So in embryonic rodent cortex, the cell that guides migrating neurons is also the cell that makes most of them.
